Prevention: Uproot and remove all weeds and all remnants of previous crop, burn or compost.
Intercrop with repellent crops, e.g. onion and garlic.
If possible, plant one repellent plant for every ten cauliflowers.
Maintain the recommended crop spacing e.g.
Kathmandu local = 60X60cm (it’s important to avoid dense planting).
Use the recommended dose of fertiliser, with a split dose of nitrogen 4.5kg
MOP/ropani as a basal dose, then 1 month after seedling transplant 5.5 kg urea/ropani.
Use routine irrigation to prevent the field becoming too dry.
Use of farm yard manure should not be done more than the recommended dose.
Monitoring: Inspect the field twice a week; look on the underside of leaves to check for egg masses and the green larvae.
On average, two medium sized larvae per ten leaves (i.e. 20% of cauliflower infested) is the minimum action threshold.
Direct Control: Hand-pick leaves with egg masses and larvae, destroy by crushing or keeping in a bucket of soapy water.
Collect and destroy adult butterflies using sweep net; do during the day when adults are active.
Azadirachtin (neem-based insecticide) @ 5 ml /lit water and 25 lit of this solution/ropani; max. 3 sprays, at 1 week intervals.
Beauveria bassiana (for e.g. ‘Daman’) 1% WP @ 5 gm /lit water and 25 lit water / ropani.
Spray late afternoon (to avoid sun); maximum three sprays, at one week interval.
Restrictions: Equipment (PPE) while mixing and applying pesticides.
Benzoate (5% SG) at a rate of 2 gm/6 lit water and 25 litre of this solution/ ropani.
Pre-harvest interval (PHI) is 3 days, If repeat applications use a minimum 15 day interval.
